mcqs.question: Why should every FORTRAN program include IMPLICIT NONE?

options.A: It makes the program run faster
options.B: It forces explicit declaration, catching typos as compile errors
options.C: It is required by the FORTRAN90 standard for all programs
options.D: It enables double precision by default

mcqs.explanation: Without IMPLICIT NONE, FORTRAN silently creates new variables from misspelled names, hiding bugs.

whyOthersWrong.A: It has no effect on runtime performance.
whyOthersWrong.C: It's strongly recommended, not mandated by the language standard.
whyOthersWrong.D: Precision is set by explicit type declarations, not by IMPLICIT NONE.

mcqs.question: What does the FORTRAN expression 1/2 evaluate to?
mcqs.explanation: Both operands are integers, so FORTRAN performs integer division, truncating to 0.

whyOthersWrong.A: 0.5 would require at least one operand to be REAL.
whyOthersWrong.C: Integer division of 1 by 2 truncates toward zero, giving 0, not 1.
whyOthersWrong.D: This is valid, if often unintended, FORTRAN code — not a compile error.

mcqs.question: What is the default index of the first element of REAL :: A(10)?
mcqs.explanation: FORTRAN arrays default to 1-based indexing, unlike C-family languages.

whyOthersWrong.A: 0-based indexing is the C/Python convention, not FORTRAN's default.
whyOthersWrong.C: Negative default indexing does not occur.
whyOthersWrong.D: The indexing convention is fixed by the declaration, not runtime-dependent.
